purpose: Highly targeted Book enrichment focused on direct experimental links from hot-runner or melt-valve control to measured moulded-part quality and process capability. Exact DOI/title searches were screened against main and the current PR before admission. All four additions belong to one broader Kazmer dynamic-melt-control research family and must not be counted as four independent experimental confirmations.

candidates.title: Consistency and Flexibility of Multi Cavity Melt Control
data: multiple dynamic valve stems installed in a hot-runner feed system for local polymer-flow control
simultaneous cavity-pressure control at multiple mould locations
commercial four-gate application
eleven measured part dimensions
reported process-capability Cp improvement between 50% and 400% across all eleven dimensions
multiple dimensions independently and simultaneously adjusted through local shrinkage control
candidates.rightsState: publisher-controlled International Polymer Processing article; use factual aggregate findings and create original Book diagrams/tables rather than reproducing protected figures
candidates.value: Rare direct quality evidence connecting distributed hot-runner melt control to multiple measured dimensions and capability, strengthening the Book's command/control -> local melt state -> part outcome chain.
candidates.limitations: Older commercial application and one broader research family; actuator architecture and reported Cp gains are system-specific and do not define modern servo-valve performance or universal control gains.

candidates.title: The process capability of multi-cavity pressure control for the injection molding process
data: dynamic valves in the melt-delivery system independently meter flow and pressure to different mould regions
experimental flow balancing and knit-line movement
multiple part dimensions controlled through distributed pressure control
testing under typical production process disturbances
reported process-capability index Cp increased from 0.52 for conventional moulding to 1.5 with closed-loop multi-cavity pressure control
candidates.rightsState: publisher-controlled Polymer Engineering & Science article; reference factual results and build original Book explanatory graphics
candidates.value: Directly links distributed melt-pressure actuation to measurable quality/capability under process disturbances instead of stopping at pressure-curve control alone.
candidates.limitations: Companion/continuation evidence from the same research family as the 1998 commercial application; Cp values are study-specific and must not be generalized to other moulds, materials or valve systems.

candidates.title: Validation of moulding consistency with a self-regulating melt pressure valve
data: two self-regulating melt-pressure valves in a hot-runner injection-moulding process
valve pin adjusts juncture loss by balancing an applied control force against melt-pressure force
resolution-IV fractional-factorial comparison with conventional hot-runner moulding
part-weight consistency used as the quality outcome
open-loop self-regulating valve reportedly reduced sensitivity of part weight to process changes by 73%
short-term part-to-part variation reportedly reduced by 60%
slower pneumatic closed-loop response could induce more variation than the open-loop self-regulating mode
candidates.rightsState: publisher-controlled Plastics, Rubber and Composites article; use factual aggregate findings and original Book diagrams
candidates.value: Adds a useful counterexample to the assumption that more closed-loop control is automatically better: actuator dynamics can worsen variation, while a pressure-responsive valve can materially change part-weight robustness.
candidates.limitations: Legacy pneumatic/self-regulating architecture and same broader Kazmer control family; no public synchronized raw valve-position/current/cavity-pressure/quality traces are exposed.

candidates.title: Validation of moulding productivity with two self-regulating melt pressure valves
data: two self-regulating melt-pressure valves independently tune two cavities of differing geometry
reported mouldings could not be produced to specification without the valves or mould-design changes
part-weight standard-deviation consistency with the self-regulating valves reported at least twice that of conventional moulding
independent melt-pressure profiling and time shifting by moulding zone
reported 20% clamp-tonnage reduction with no cycle-time increase
reported 50% clamp-tonnage reduction with an 8% cycle-time increase
candidates.rightsState: publisher-controlled Plastics, Rubber and Composites article; use factual aggregate values and create original Book trade-off tables
candidates.value: Connects local melt-pressure control not only to quality consistency but to an explicit clamp-tonnage/cycle-time trade-off, useful for teaching that process robustness and productivity objectives can interact.
candidates.limitations: Same 2004 valve platform and broader research family as the consistency paper; reported productivity trade-offs are case-specific and are not safe generic clamp-reduction targets.
